news.title: AFC Champions League Elite: Wissing Says Al-Ittihad Ready for Al-Ain Clash
news.og_title: AFC Champions League Elite: Wissing Says Al-Ittihad Ready for Al-Ain Clash
news.og_desc:
Jeddah, November 01, 2026, SPA -- Al-Ittihad head coach Jens Wissing said his side is ready for Monday's clash with the UAE's Al-Ain in matchday four of the 2026–2027 AFC Champions League Elite. The team aims to demonstrate its character and secure a positive result.
    Speaking at a press conference at Al-Ittihad's headquarters on Sunday, Wissing said the match would be a challenge against a strong opponent. He added that preparations had gone well, with one final training session remaining before Monday's match. Wissing noted that Al-Ain has quality players but stressed that Al-Ittihad also has the talent and resources to deliver the expected level of performance.
    He said the team continues to develop and has reached a good level, although there is still a long way to go. He added that the team has ambitions and goals to achieve and that the players understand what is required of them at this stage.
    Asked about the decision to play with one striker and the rotation policy, Wissing said the team has several attacking options, including George, Youssef, and Saleh. He praised the cooperation among the forwards and their support for one another. He also noted that managing players' workloads is part of his coaching responsibilities. With the team having played 17 matches so far, he said it is difficult for any one player to feature in every game. Player selection depends on the technical considerations and circumstances of each match.
    Regarding two injured players, Wissing said Doumbia has been training on the pitch for some time. He added that both players are making considerable efforts to regain full fitness and expressed hope that they would rejoin team training in the coming period.
    For his part, Al-Ittihad player Mukhtar Ali said the team is eager to win and dedicate the victory to its fans while delivering a performance worthy of their expectations. He said the players understand their responsibility and that winning is the least they can offer their supporters. He also expressed hope for a strong turnout and enthusiastic support from fans during the match.
    Asked about his comfort playing in midfield, Mukhtar said he feels the head coach's confidence, as do all the players. He added that a better understanding of the coach's tactical approach gives him greater confidence on the pitch. He reaffirmed his commitment to giving his best and helping the team secure victory.
    -- SPA
